# Document

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

High-level entry point for creating PDF documents. Provides a simplified API for adding elements, setting metadata, and saving PDFs.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

## Constructors

```typescript
new Document()
new Document(options: DocumentOptions)
new Document(settings: DocumentSettings)
new Document(metadata: DocumentMetadata)
new Document(settings: DocumentSettings, metadata: DocumentMetadata)
```

## Properties

- [`attachments`](#attachments): Files embedded into the generated PDF as associated files (PDF/A-3 / ZUGFeRD).
- [`diagnostics`](#diagnostics): Recoverable issues collected during the most recent `generateBytes` / `generateBytesAsync` call - typically font load failures or subset fallbacks.
- [`fonts`](#fonts): The fonts that belong to this document: any number of families and faces.
- [`metadata`](#metadata): Document metadata: title, author, subject, keywords and similar descriptive fields.

- [`settings`](#settings): Document settings: version, conformance, accessibility, security and similar choices that apply to the whole file.
- [`svgRasterizer`](#svgrasterizer): The registered SVG rasterizer, if any; see `registerSvgRasterizer`.

### `attachments`

```typescript
readonly attachments: readonly FileAttachment[]
```

*read-only*

Files embedded into the generated PDF as associated files (PDF/A-3 / ZUGFeRD). Embedded files are honoured under `None`, PDF/A-3 and PDF/A-4f; under PDF/A-1, PDF/A-2 and PDF/A-4 they are dropped at generation time with a diagnostic, keeping the conformance claim honest. Under PDF/UA-2, an attachment with no `description` is described by its file name and records a warning.

A read-only array: read it or loop over it. It has no `add` or `push`; add a file with [`Document.attach`](document.md#attach).

Example:

```typescript
doc.attach({ fileName: 'data.csv', content: bytes, relationship: AttachmentRelationship.Data, mediaType: 'text/csv' });
console.log(doc.attachments.length); // 1
```

### `diagnostics`

```typescript
readonly diagnostics: readonly IDiagnostic[]
```

*read-only*

Recoverable issues collected during the most recent `generateBytes` / `generateBytesAsync` call - typically font load failures or subset fallbacks. Empty before generation. Call `printDiagnostics` to surface them via console, or inspect directly to feed into custom UI / telemetry.

> A read-only list: read it or loop over it, but it has no `add` or `push`.

### `fonts`

```typescript
readonly fonts: DocumentFonts
```

*read-only*

The fonts that belong to this document: any number of families and faces. Nothing added here is visible to another document, and the global font registries are unchanged. A family named here is resolved before the global and standard ones.

Example:

```typescript
doc.fonts.add(regularBytes, { family: 'Inter' });
doc.fonts.add(boldBytes, { family: 'Inter', weight: 'bold' });
doc.add(new TextBlock({ text: 'Hello', fontFamily: 'Inter', fontWeight: 'bold' }));
```

## Methods

- [`add`](#add): Adds an element to the current (last) page.
- [`addPage`](#addpage): Adds a new page using the document's default size and margin.
- [`addRange`](#addrange): Adds multiple elements to the current page.
- [`attach`](#attach): Embeds a file into the document.
- [`dispose`](#dispose): Releases the pages held by the document.
- [`generateBytes`](#generatebytes): Serializes the document to PDF bytes synchronously.
- [`generateBytesAsync`](#generatebytesasync): Serializes the document to PDF bytes asynchronously.
- [`generateFirstPageSvgAsync`](#generatefirstpagesvgasync): Convenience for example cards and social previews: renders the first page to a standalone SVG string.
- [`generateSvgDocumentAsync`](#generatesvgdocumentasync): Like `generateSvgPagesAsync`, but also returns `@font-face` CSS that embeds a minimal subset of the fonts the document uses.
- [`generateSvgPageAsync`](#generatesvgpageasync): Renders a single page (zero-based index) to a standalone SVG string.
- [`generateSvgPagesAsync`](#generatesvgpagesasync): Renders every laid-out page of the document to a standalone SVG string.
- [`printDiagnostics`](#printdiagnostics): Convenience: writes each diagnostic to `console.error` / `console.warn` / `console.info` according to its severity.
- [`registerSvgRasterizer`](#registersvgrasterizer): Registers a function that renders SVG markup to PNG bytes, or removes it with `undefined`.
- [`save`](#save): Saves the document to the given file path synchronously.
- [`saveAsync`](#saveasync): Saves the document to the given file path asynchronously via the configured platform I/O.
- [`setCurrentPageSettings`](#setcurrentpagesettings): Replaces the current (last) page with a new page of the given settings, preserving any elements already added to it.

### `add`

```typescript
add(element: IElement | string | readonly string[]): void
```

Adds an element to the current (last) page.

Example:

```typescript
const doc = new Document();
doc.add(new TextBlock('Quarterly report', { fontSize: 20 }));
doc.add(new TextBlock('Prepared by Operations'));
```

### `addPage`

```typescript
addPage(): Page
addPage(options: AddPageOptions): Page
addPage(pageSize: PdfSize): Page
addPage(pageSize: PdfSize, margin: number): Page
addPage(pageSize: PdfSize, orientation: PageOrientation): Page
addPage(pageSize: PdfSize, orientation: PageOrientation, margin: number): Page
```

Adds a new page using the document's default size and margin.

Example:

```typescript
const doc = new Document();
doc.add(new TextBlock('First page'));
doc.addPage(); // start a new page
doc.add(new TextBlock('Second page'));
```

Example:

```typescript
doc.addPage({ orientation: PageOrientation.Landscape, margin: 30 })
```

### `addRange`

```typescript
addRange(elements: Iterable<IElement>): void
```

Adds multiple elements to the current page.

Example:

```typescript
doc.addRange([new TextBlock('One'), new TextBlock('Two'), new TextBlock('Three')]);
```

### `attach`

```typescript
attach(attachment: FileAttachment): Document
attach(fileName: string, content: Uint8Array, options?: { relationship?: AttachmentRelationship; mediaType?: string; }): Document
```

Embeds a file into the document. Returns this document for chaining.

Example:

```typescript
doc.attach({ fileName: 'invoice.xml', content: xmlBytes, relationship: AttachmentRelationship.Alternative, mediaType: 'text/xml' });
```

Example:

```typescript
doc.attach('data.csv', bytes, { relationship: AttachmentRelationship.Data, mediaType: 'text/csv' });
```

### `dispose`

```typescript
dispose(): void
```

Releases the pages held by the document. Calling it again has no effect; adding to a disposed document throws.

Example, from `code-recipes/fonts/font-fallback`:

```typescript
doc.dispose();
```

Example, from `code-recipes/compliance-archival/document-diagnostics`:

```typescript
draft.dispose();
```

### `generateBytes`

```typescript
generateBytes(): Uint8Array
```

Serializes the document to PDF bytes synchronously.

Embedded TrueType fonts are loaded with `TtfFont.fromFileSync()`, which requires a Node.js environment.  In browser contexts call `generateBytesAsync()` instead so fonts are fetched via the Fetch API.

Fully synchronous - uses the RC4 encryption path if encryption is set (AES-256 encryption requires saveAsync).

Example:

```typescript
const bytes = doc.generateBytes(); // Node only
```

### `generateBytesAsync`

```typescript
generateBytesAsync(options?: GenerateOptions): Promise<Uint8Array>
```

Serializes the document to PDF bytes asynchronously.

Uses a two-phase render: 1. A quick dry-run to discover every embedded font referenced by the document. 2. An async preload step that fetches TTF bytes via the configured platform I/O (works in both Node.js and browser environments when `configurePlatform(new BrowserPlatformIO())` has been called). 3. The real render pass, which uses the loaded fonts to emit correct GID hex strings in content streams.

Prefer this over `generateBytes()` whenever TTF font embedding is used in a browser context.

Example:

```typescript
const bytes = await doc.generateBytesAsync();

// Cancel with an AbortSignal:
const controller = new AbortController();
const pending = doc.generateBytesAsync({ signal: controller.signal });
controller.abort();
```

### `generateFirstPageSvgAsync`

```typescript
generateFirstPageSvgAsync(options?: SvgPageExportOptions): Promise<string>
```

Convenience for example cards and social previews: renders the first page to a standalone SVG string.

### `generateSvgDocumentAsync`

```typescript
generateSvgDocumentAsync(options?: SvgPageExportOptions): Promise<SvgDocumentExport>
```

Like `generateSvgPagesAsync`, but also returns `@font-face` CSS that embeds a minimal subset of the fonts the document uses. Inject the CSS once into the host page so the SVG renders with the exact fonts used for layout, independent of what the viewer has installed. See [`SvgDocumentExport`](svg-document-export.md).

### `generateSvgPageAsync`

```typescript
generateSvgPageAsync(pageIndex: number, options?: SvgPageExportOptions): Promise<string>
```

Renders a single page (zero-based index) to a standalone SVG string.

### `generateSvgPagesAsync`

```typescript
generateSvgPagesAsync(options?: SvgPageExportOptions): Promise<string[]>
```

Renders every laid-out page of the document to a standalone SVG string.

Runs the same layout, pagination, watermark, and header/footer pipeline as PDF output, so the returned array has one entry per generated PDF page and the visual layout matches. Embedded fonts and PNG images are preloaded exactly as the async PDF path does, so this is the recommended export entry point in both Node and the browser.

Example:

```typescript
const pages = await doc.generateSvgPagesAsync({ maxPages: 1 });
document.body.innerHTML = pages[0];
```

### `printDiagnostics`

```typescript
printDiagnostics(): void
```

Convenience: writes each diagnostic to `console.error` / `console.warn` / `console.info` according to its severity. Library code never calls this implicitly - callers opt in.

### `registerSvgRasterizer`

```typescript
registerSvgRasterizer(rasterizer: SvgRasterizer | undefined): void
```

Registers a function that renders SVG markup to PNG bytes, or removes it with `undefined`.

With one registered, an [`Svg`](svg.md) element whose `strictUnsupportedFeatures` is `false` draws what the SVG importer cannot draw as vector content - filters, masks, stylesheets, … - as images in their place, instead of skipping them. BonniePDF rasterizes nothing itself: any renderer will do. It is called on the async generate paths only; a synchronous generate whose document would need it fails rather than drawing something different.

### `save`

```typescript
save(path: string): void
```

Saves the document to the given file path synchronously. Requires a platform with synchronous file IO (Node.js via the node entry point); throws in browser contexts - use saveAsync instead.

### `saveAsync`

```typescript
saveAsync(path: string, options?: GenerateOptions): Promise<void>
```

Saves the document to the given file path asynchronously via the configured platform I/O. Uses the async generation path, so embedded fonts are preloaded (browser-safe) and AES-256 encryption is supported.

Example:

```typescript
await doc.saveAsync('./report.pdf'); // Node; in a browser use generateBytesAsync()
```

### `setCurrentPageSettings`

```typescript
setCurrentPageSettings(pageSize: PdfSize, orientation: PageOrientation, margin: number): void
```

Replaces the current (last) page with a new page of the given settings, preserving any elements already added to it.
